pr_title: promql: Fall back to full label sets when sorting by label
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/14289. 

Fall back to comparing by full label sets instead of sample values in `sort_by_label` and `sort_by_label_desc`.

We considered falling back to hashed label sets. However, `Labels.Hash()` methods have different implementations depending on the build tag. Their output differs accordingly. This would make the expected order in tests depend on the build tag as well.

issue_context.title: promql: sort_by_label should fallback to a consistent ordering by metric, not by sample value
issue_context.body:
### Proposal

I got an idea while thinking about https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/12503 : 

Currently, if `sort_by_label` encounters the same label values to sort by, it falls back to sorting by sample value. However, by using `sort_by_label`, the user essentially tells us they aren't interested in the sample value, but in label values.

I guess it would be more useful to use the rest of the metric (label values, name) as the "tie breaker" rather than the sample value. It doesn't even have to be a particular order, as long as the tie breaker yields consistent results, i.e. we could just use the metric hash as the tiebreaker rather than the sample value.

In other words, the sorting would always be the same, even if sample values change.
comments:
I can't think how it can happen that two series have the same label value.
The PromQL engine checks between each operation and halts with an error if it finds this case.

However I agree it is a nice optimisation, to avoid doing work that cannot be useful.
Oh, my mistake - it sorts by a subset of labels, which can have the same value.
May I please be assigned to this issue?
